item.description:
Shipdeck 0.7.3 beta (26)

  • Product statuses by stage, warnings that follow the status, store-required updates
  • Agents push the store listing draft; pick checklist items with todos; keep the Mac awake
  • App Store Connect phase 2: TestFlight, store listing, screenshots, pricing, IAPs, sales
  • Release checklist: Work with Claude on every open item

Shipdeck 0.7.2

  • Try new builds early. Turn on Settings › General › Get Beta Updates to be offered test builds before they become a regular release. They may have bugs; turn it off to wait for the next regular release.

Shipdeck 0.7.1

  • See what is left before a release. When an app's repo is ahead of the store, the Roadmap tab starts with that version's checklist. It lists Shipdeck's steps that aren't on it yet (Add Them in one click), shows the next step with the button that does it, and the todos planned for that version.
  • Work on roadmap items with Claude. Every todo, and every checklist item Claude can do in the repo, has Work with Claude…. Choose Select to pick several todos and work on them in one session. Claude reads the code and agrees a plan with you before changing anything, and asks you to approve marking each item done.

Shipdeck 0.7.0

  • Group and sort the sidebar. Products are grouped by status (In development, Released, Maintenance…) and sorted by when you last opened them. Change either one from the menu at the foot of the sidebar: no grouping, or sort by name or by what needs attention.
  • Create the App Store Connect app, then link it. Registering an App ID doesn't create the app, and Apple's API can't. When a component has no app yet, the App Store tab shows the name, bundle ID and SKU to enter, each with a copy button, a link to App Store Connect's New App page, and Create with Claude…, which fills the form in your browser with Claude in Chrome and waits for your OK before creating it.
  • New apps show up for linking. The list of App Store Connect apps is read again when you come back to Shipdeck, and from Reload Apps, instead of staying as it was when Shipdeck started.

Shipdeck 0.6.9

  • Register App IDs from Shipdeck. The App Store tab lists each iOS or macOS app's App ID: whether its bundle ID is registered, and which capabilities its entitlements use (Push Notifications, Game Center, Sign in with Apple, iCloud…) that aren't enabled yet. Register the App ID or enable what is missing after a confirmation, even before the app exists in App Store Connect. The release checklist checks both.
  • Agents can do it too, within limits. Claude sessions get asc.appIDs, asc.registerAppID and asc.enableCapabilities. They only reach the product's own bundle IDs, their input is checked before you are asked to approve, and a misspelled field in any action is refused instead of being ignored.
  • Claude sessions are named after their topic. A session's tab, the menu bar and the activity feed show what the conversation is about. Double-click or right-click a tab to rename it.
  • Product icons follow the repo. When an app's icon file changes, Shipdeck shows the new icon instead of the one it saved before.

Shipdeck 0.6.8

  • A new icon. The same >_ sailboat, now in Claude's orange (Shipdeck runs on Claude Code), with a pure white glyph and a clearer hull.
  • New sites and links are checked right away. A website added by Sync with Code, or a link you change, is opened on the next refresh instead of up to 30 minutes later.
  • Fewer false "unreleased" commits. An app at the top of a repo no longer counts commits in folders that belong to other components, such as a landing page in site/.

Shipdeck 0.6.7

  • Is the site really live? Shipdeck now opens the production URL of every website, web app and backend every 30 minutes, no account needed. It tells a working site ("Live · Vercel") from a domain that forwards to another site, doesn't resolve or answers with an error, and reads the HTTPS certificate, the page's title, description, share image and icon, and an optional Health Check URL.
  • Every product's links are checked. The landing page, privacy policy, terms of use (a new link field) and support pages are opened too. For a released app, a broken link or a site that stops answering goes into a new red group, Something's Wrong. Before release, the Roadmap's checklist reports it instead.
  • Fix with Claude. Each of these problems, in the Overview and in the release checklist, has a button that opens a Claude session told what Shipdeck saw. Claude fixes what lives in the repo and gives you the exact steps for DNS and hosting dashboards.
  • A Web block in the release checklist for products with a website or web app: production URL, domain, HTTPS, page details, health check, privacy page and live. New checks now join checklists you laid out before, without starting over; ones you removed stay removed.
  • New folders aren't missed. A folder that isn't committed yet (like a new landing page) now marks the product's info as out of date, and Sync with Code shows it to Claude.

Shipdeck 0.6.6

  • A real release checklist for iOS and Android. The Roadmap's checklist is now split by platform (General, iOS · App Store, Android · Google Play) and by phase, from preparing the accounts to submitting. A first release gets the full list (age rating, App Privacy, Data safety, closed testing…), an app already on the store gets the short update list. Each item fits on one line; click it for why it's needed and a link to Apple's or Google's docs.
  • Shipdeck ticks what it can check. It reads the repo (Godot export presets, Flutter and Gradle settings, Xcode settings, icon size), your links and App Store Connect (age rating, category, store text, screenshots, App Review contact, encryption), and puts what's wrong in "To Fix First". Items Google Play would answer say so until it has a connector.
  • About the product. Answer a few questions (in-app purchases, accounts, ads, kids…) with chips, or let Claude answer them from the code, and items that don't apply step aside. You can also mark any item "Not applicable".

Shipdeck 0.6.5

  • See which product needs you. The sidebar shows each product's open sessions in a green pill. When Claude asks for permission or a choice, or an agent's action waits in the approval inbox, the pill turns orange, the product says "Waiting for you", and the session's tab and the menu bar item show it too. It clears as soon as you answer in the terminal. Works in Claude sessions opened after updating.

Shipdeck 0.6.4

  • New releases show up sooner. When a component's version in the repo is ahead of its live version, Shipdeck checks the App Store listing and the Sparkle appcast every 10 minutes instead of every 6 hours. A release you just shipped no longer shows its own commits as unreleased for hours.

Shipdeck 0.6.3

  • A Roadmap tab for every product. It follows the product's status. For an idea, it lists the specs in your repos (docs/specs/, PRD.md…) with their status, and Brainstorm with Claude… works one out with you and saves it there. In development, it shows a release checklist: Add Standard Checks adds the usual steps (commit, push, version, TestFlight build, screenshots, store text, privacy…) and Shipdeck ticks the ones it can check itself. Once released, it lists todos grouped by the version they're planned for.
  • Suggest with Claude… asks Claude to read the code and propose checklist items or todos. Like every change an agent makes to the roadmap, they wait for your approval.
  • Claude's input stays in view. Claude sessions use Claude Code's full-screen mode, so the input stays at the bottom while you scroll back. Hold Shift to select text. You can turn it off in Settings › General.

Shipdeck 0.6.2

  • Clearer first run. If Claude Code is too old for Shipdeck, the welcome screen says so and shows the command to update it. If Apple's Command Line Tools (git) are missing, it offers to install them instead of letting macOS ask again and again.
  • A survey that fails says why. The error now includes what Claude Code reported.
  • A login shell that never answers no longer leaves the Claude Code check spinning: it gives up after 20 seconds and says what to look at.
  • Help › Send Feedback… opens a feedback form with your Shipdeck and macOS versions filled in. The welcome screen says where your data goes.

Shipdeck 0.6.1

  • Sync with Code. When a product's details fall behind its repos, choose Sync with Code… (on the product's page, in the "May Be Out of Date" notice, or by right-clicking it in the sidebar). Claude re-reads the repos, starting from what Shipdeck has and what changed since the last survey, and changes no files.
  • You choose what to keep. Each change shows the old and new value and where Claude found it. Tick the ones to keep and save, or choose Edit Before Saving… to change anything else first. Things Claude no longer finds start unticked, and nothing is saved until you decide.
  • Agents ask before editing a product's details. When a Claude session wants to change a product's description, components, services or docs, the request lists each change and waits for you.
  • The line at the bottom of a product's page now reads "Auto-checked at…": Shipdeck checks git, versions and store listings on its own, without AI.

Shipdeck 0.6.0

  • Approve what agents do on the App Store. When a Claude session wants to reply to a review, pause, resume or finish a phased release, or release a version, the request appears at the top of the window with the details (for a reply, the review and the full text), on the menu bar and as a notification. Choose Allow Once, Deny (with a reason the agent reads), or Always Allow in the product.
  • Always Allow stays small. It only covers changes that can be taken back, such as review replies and pausing a phased release, and only in that product. Releases ask every time. Settings › Agents lists what you allowed and lets you take it back.
  • Activity shows which actions you approved. A request nobody answers is withdrawn after 10 minutes, or when its session closes.

Shipdeck 0.5.0

  • Claude sessions can work with Shipdeck. Each Claude session now starts with Shipdeck's tools (an MCP server), and every session has a shipdeck command. An agent can read its product, what needs attention, unreleased commits and the App Store Connect status (versions, builds, TestFlight, reviews), change the product's status and open or close sessions.
  • Each session stays in its own product. A session can only read and change the product it belongs to, and only that product's App Store Connect apps, even when other apps share the same account. Adding keys, linking apps and removing products stay with you.
  • Anything that reaches Apple needs you. Releasing, phased releases and review replies are refused for agents until Shipdeck can ask for your approval, which comes next.
  • Activity. The product page lists what you and its sessions changed, including refused attempts and why.

Shipdeck 0.4.5

  • Adding an App Store Connect key works. Settings › Accounts › Add Key… shows the Name, private key, Key ID, Issuer ID and Role fields again, instead of only the instructions.

Shipdeck 0.4.4

  • Tabs fit again. Switching from a product with two tabs to one with an App Store tab no longer leaves the Overview, App Store and Sessions tabs cut off in the toolbar.

Shipdeck 0.4.3

  • Everything on the Overview. The product info panel is gone: its description, out-of-date notice, repos, services, docs and links now sit on the product's Overview, so the terminal gets the full width in Sessions.
  • Change the status in place. Click the status badge next to the product's name to mark it Released, Maintenance or anything else, without opening Edit Details.
  • Live versions of Mac apps. Mac apps that update through Sparkle now show their live version and its date, read from the app's appcast, with a link to its releases. Unreleased commits count from that version.

Shipdeck 0.4.2

  • Every change since your version. When you skip a few updates, the update window now lists what's new in each version since the one you have, not just the newest.

Shipdeck 0.4.1

  • Maintenance release. Nothing changes in the app. This version checks that updates keep arriving after the release process was made more reliable.

Shipdeck 0.4.0

  • App Store Connect in each product. Products with an iOS app get an App Store tab: where the next version is in App Review, the live version and its phased release, TestFlight builds, groups and tester feedback, and customer reviews with Apple's summary. A product can have several iOS apps; pick one at the top of the tab.
  • Release and reply from Shipdeck. Release an approved version, pause, resume or finish a phased release, and reply to reviews. Each action asks you to confirm first.
  • Accounts. Add an App Store Connect team key in Settings › Accounts. Its private key is stored in your login keychain. Each product links to one account, and its apps are matched by bundle ID.
  • More in Needs Attention. The overview now shows rejected versions, versions waiting for you to release, paused phased releases, failed builds, unanswered reviews and new TestFlight crashes.
  • Fixes. Closing a terminal whose shell ignores the hangup now ends it after 5 seconds (it took about 12). Saving a product no longer keeps an empty store entry.

Shipdeck 0.3.0

  • In-app updates. Shipdeck checks for new versions once a day and offers to install them. You can also choose Check for Updates… in the app menu or the menu bar item. Updates are signed, and Shipdeck verifies them before installing.
  • Icons from Icon Composer. Products whose app icon is an Icon Composer document (AppIcon.icon, the Liquid Glass format) now show it, Shipdeck included. With Xcode installed it renders with the glass effects; without Xcode Shipdeck builds a flat version.

Coming from 0.2.0 or earlier, install this version by hand once: quit Shipdeck, download the zip, and replace the app in Applications. Later versions arrive in the app.
